model.name: binomial logistic regression with log10 female and male gametocyte densities

asexual_assessment.interpretation: Adding log10 asexual density did not improve out-of-sample log loss, so it was not retained as a useful predictor in the simplest defensible model.

calibration.interpretation: Calibration was close to ideal (intercept near 0, slope near 1), with no strong evidence of systematic under- or overprediction.

literature.claim: Separate female and male gametocyte densities predict mosquito infection better than total gametocyte density alone.
literature.citation: Andolina C, Churcher TS, et al. Predicting the likelihood and intensity of mosquito infection from sex-specific Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte density. eLife. 2018.

literature.claim: Pfs25 and PfMGET are validated sex-specific qRT-PCR markers for female and male Plasmodium falciparum gametocytes.
literature.citation: Schneider P, et al. Quantification of female and male Plasmodium falciparum gametocytes by reverse transcriptase quantitative PCR. Molecular and Biochemical Parasitology. 2015.

literature.claim: SBP1 is a sensitive qRT-PCR marker for low-density Plasmodium falciparum asexual parasites.
literature.citation: Tadesse FG, et al. Molecular markers for sensitive detection of Plasmodium falciparum asexual stage parasites and their application in a malaria clinical trial. Am J Trop Med Hyg. 2017.
